jobs.title: Supply Chain Program Manager
jobs.description:
As a Supply Chain Program Manager in the Supply Chain Center of Excellence, you will work alongside some of the most experienced and accomplished minds across Western Digital's Supply Chain functions, while engaging with the newest and most cutting-edge ideas in the field. Your role is to bring the two together, combining proven expertise with emerging thinking so that they work in harmony and deliver results.
You will be awarded opportunities across the full spectrum of Supply Chain functions, engaging with established leaders in Logistics, Direct Procurement, Indirect Procurement, Planning, Risk and Resiliency, Operations and beyond. Rather than relying on authority, you will build consensus through influence and persuasion, grounded in both hard facts and qualitative insight. Success depends on strong dependency management, stakeholder alignment and clear communication across functions that may have other priorities.
How we Operate
These are the behaviors expected every day. They map to the WD Leadership Expectations and define the standard that this position role models for the wider team.
- Own the outcome, not the tracker. The plan is an instrument. The measure is whether the ramp landed on time, at cost and at quality.
- Champion clear decisions. Most Program delay is undecided, not unknown. Frame the choice, name the decider, get it made and record it.
- Manage the seams. Functions are usually competent inside their own boundary. Programs fail between them, which is where the Program Manager works.
- Escalate early with a recommendation. Raise it when there is still room to act, and bring the option you would choose.
- Be direct and transparent about status. Green that turns red without warning destroys credibility permanently. Report what is, not what is hoped.
- Influence without direct line authority. Nobody on the Program reports to you. Credibility, preparation and reliability are the only levers — build them deliberately.
- Close the loop. A Program that ends without lessons captured has spent the organization’s learning and kept none of it

Key Responsibilities
Strong Program Management Skills
- Integrated planning and governance. Own the master plan, milestones, dependencies, owners, RAID log and steering committee cadence across all workstreams, with an independent view of status.
- Scope, schedule and budget control. Protect the baseline, manage change through a disciplined process, and keep the program on time and on budget.
- Risk and decision management. Surface risks early, frame decisions with options and a recommendation, and record outcomes so they are not relitigated.
- Run the Program cadence at the right rhythm for the phase
- Maintain a single source of truth for Program status
- Define and enforce entry and exit criteria at each gate

Program Portfolio Leadership and Team Development
- Own a portfolio of supply chain Programs, including major ramps and transitions of high complexity
- Lead, coach and develop the Program Managers running them, building advanced proficiency across the Program management toolkit
- Set the Program management standard for the function: plans, cadence, gates, reporting and post-Program review
- Frame executive decisions, manage complex risk and drive cross-functional alignment without authority

Stakeholder Alignment
- Cross-functional alignment. Bring together Legal, Direct Materials, Indirect Procurement, Logistics, Sales, Finance and IT, each with different contract types, risk tolerances and priorities.
- Balancing competing priorities. Reconcile Legal’s risk posture, Procurement’s efficiency goals and the business’s need for speed into decisions all parties can support.
- Composure with difficult stakeholders. Remain calm, respectful and fact-based when challenged; depersonalize conflict and keep the focus on outcomes.
- Earned trust and sponsorship. Involve skeptics early, give them a real voice in design, and use executive sponsors and escalation paths deliberately.

Cross-Functional Dependency Management
- Map dependencies across Sourcing, Engineering, Quality, Operations, Planning and suppliers
- Track dependency status and drive owners to their commitments
- Resolve cross-functional conflicts at the working level where possible
- Escalate blocked dependencies with the decision required clearly stated

Risk and Decision Management
- Maintain a live Program risk register with owners, mitigations and trigger points
- Run scenario analysis on the risks that could move the Program
- Frame decisions clearly: the choice, the options, the trade-offs, the recommendation, the decider
- Track decisions and their rationale so they are not relitigated

Delivery and Adoption Discipline
- Fit to standard. Champion out-of-the-box capability and challenge customization that adds cost and risk without clear value.
- Testing and cutover. Lead system integration and user acceptance testing, data migration validation and a well-rehearsed go-live.
- Adoption and value. Drive training, change champions and adoption metrics such as contract cycle time, and confirm the business case is realized.
- Measure adoption and sustainment, and reinforce new behaviors until they become the way Western Digital works

Change management
- Lead organizational change that turns new processes, tools and ways of working into lasting habits across the enterprise
- Build a compelling case for change and inspire stakeholders at every level, from executive sponsors to frontline teams
- Design adoption roadmaps with clear communication, training and engagement plans that bring people along, not just systems
- Identify and empower change champions who carry new practices into their own functions and regions
- Anticipate resistance early and turn skeptics into advocates through listening, evidence and quick wins

Executive Communication and Decision Framing
- Report Program status honestly, concisely and consistently
- Frame executive decisions with the choice, options, trade-offs and a recommendation
- Run executive forums that produce decisions rather than updates
- Manage expectations early rather than explaining misses afterwards
- Executive communication. Deliver concise, candid status that lets sponsors act quickly and with confidence.
- Governance.  Run a structured governance process to include daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly core team and steering Committee meetings
- Collateral development. Create update templates and work individually and with team members to create executive communication collateral

Program Analytics and Reporting
- Build and maintain readiness and status dashboards
- Use data rather than narrative to drive Program conversations
- Track leading indicators, not just milestone completion
- Adopt tooling, automation, and AI that reduce reporting effort

Post-Program Learning
- Run honest post-Program reviews covering what worked and what did not
- Convert lessons into process change with the relevant process owner
- Share learning across the Program community
- Improve templates, gates and standards based on what was learned

Business Process Transformation
- Champion innovation by challenging how work is done today and envisioning how it should be done tomorrow
- Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize and digitize end-to-end business processes across supply chain functions
- Oversee transformation projects from concept through delivery, ensuring they meet scope, schedule and value commitments
- Partner with IT and business owners to align process redesign with enabling systems, data and AI capabilities
- Measure the impact of each transformation and feed the lessons into the next wave of improvement

What would success look like
- Big bets that land. Bold programs and transformations delivered on time, on budget and at the quality customers expect.
- Problems solved before they surface. Risks and gaps spotted early and closed well ahead of the moment they could hurt the business.
- A supply chain ready for what's next. Capacity, capability and technology in place before demand arrives, not after.
- Change without chaos. New processes, tools and transitions rolled out smoothly, with no disruption to customers and no value left on the table.
- A voice leaders trust. Reporting so candid and reliable that there are never surprises, and status always reflects reality.
- Decisions made in the room. Choices framed so clearly that leaders can act on the spot and keep momentum high.
- A legacy that compounds. Every lesson turned into a lasting standard, so each program makes the next one faster, smarter and better.
Required
- Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Engineering, Business or a related field
- 10+ years of experience in supply chain, operations or program management, including leading product ramps, technology transitions or supplier readiness in a high-tech, semiconductor or electronics manufacturing environment
- A track record of leading process improvement or transformation work with measurable results
- Hands-on familiarity with AI and automation, including generative AI tools, and the curiosity to apply them to real supply chain problems
- Organizational change management experience
- Experience leading and developing Program Managers or cross-functional teams
- Demonstrated ability to frame executive decisions and influence senior stakeholders without direct authority
- Strong working knowledge of supplier capacity, qualification, engineering change and end-of-life management
- Proficiency with program analytics and dashboarding tools

Preferred
- Master's degree or MBA
- PMP, PgMP or ASCM (APICS) certification
- Experience in data storage or hard disk drive supply chains
- Delivering AI and machine learning use cases, such as predictive supplier risk, demand sensing and generative AI assistants
- Experience with control towers, digital twins and supplier risk platforms
- Setting up or maturing a Program Management Office, which ties to the next-generation PMO in the opening
- Leading scenario planning, tabletop exercises or business continuity programs
- A background in consulting, transformation offices or a center of excellence
- Familiarity with sustainability, ESG and trade-compliance requirements
- Working with global teams and Asia-based supplier networks
- Change management certification (e.g., Prosci) or a record of leading large-scale adoption programs

Programs are where every part of the supply chain organization has to work as one. This role holds limited authority and all of the accountability, which makes credibility the entire currency of the role. Earn it by being prepared, being honest about status, and forcing the decisions nobody else wants to call.
In summary, the Program Manager is encouraged to bring innovation and creativity to every challenge, and fresh thinking about where the supply chain should go next will always be welcome. You will not be starting from a blank page: Western Digital is already pursuing a number of cutting-edge initiatives, and you will have the opportunity to shape, accelerate and expand them.

jobs.title: Talent Program Manager (APAC)
jobs.description:
The Early Career Talent Program Manager will play a critical role in executing and enhancing our early career strategy across the Asia-Pacific region. Based in Singapore, this role partners closely with global program leadership to deliver high-impact internship and full-time early career programs, while tailoring execution to meet regional market needs.
This role blends program management and enablement, requiring a strong operator who can also build scalable frameworks, tools, and resources to empower regional stakeholders. The Program Manager will oversee the full lifecycle of early career programs, including onboarding, development, engagement, and offboarding, while enabling consistent, high-quality experiences across countries such as Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore and broader APAC markets.
Success in this role requires strong cross-cultural collaboration, operational rigor, stakeholder partnership, and the ability to translate global strategy into locally relevant execution. This role will require travel to support program delivery, events, and key milestones.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Program Strategy, Enablement & Regional Alignment
- Execute and localize global early career program strategies across APAC, ensuring alignment with regional business needs and workforce planning

- Build and continuously improve program enablement tools, playbooks, and resources to support managers, mentors, and regional stakeholders

- Partner with Recruiting, HRBPs, and business leaders across APAC to align hiring, onboarding, and program delivery

- Establish scalable frameworks to ensure consistency while allowing for regional customization across countries

Program Execution & Operations
- Lead end-to-end delivery of internship and full-time early career programs across APAC, including onboarding, orientation, learning sessions, engagement events, and offboarding

- Manage program logistics including event planning, vendor coordination, scheduling, and budget tracking

- Track participant progress, engagement, and performance in alignment with the global program strategy

- Serve as a primary point of contact for early career hires, interns, and managers across the region

- Travel to key APAC locations as needed to support in-person program execution and events

Engagement, Facilitation & Communications
- Deliver engaging, relevant programming that fosters belonging, development, and connection

- Facilitate workshops, onboarding sessions, and live events

- Partner with Talent Brand to support program branding and regional awareness

- Ensure clear, consistent communication across interns, full-time hires, managers, mentors, and business leaders

- Act as a visible and trusted program leader, driving a high-energy, cohesive experience across the region
- 5+ years of experience in program management, early career programs, university recruiting, or talent development
- Proven experience managing early career programs across APAC, with strong familiarity with early career talent programming across key APAC markets; including, Thailand, Malaysia, and Singapore
- Demonstrated experience balancing program execution and enablement, including building tools, frameworks, or scalable processes
- Strong program management skills, including planning, execution, stakeholder management, and program effectiveness measurement
- Experience working cross-functionally with recruiting, HR, learning & development, talent brand, and business stakeholders
- Strong facilitation and presentation skills, with comfort engaging both early career audiences and senior leaders
- Ability to operate effectively in a regional, cross-cultural environment
- Willingness and flexibility to travel as needed

jobs.title: Vice President, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
The Vice President of Financial Planning and Analysis will serve as the primary finance leader for setting the strategic vision and direction of the FP&A organization. Reporting into the SVP Corporate Finance, this leader will partner with the executive leadership team in developing, tracking and optimizing WD’s financial performance. This leader will lead the development of the company’s short and long-range financial plans, annual operating plans, quarterly forecasts, short-and long-term operating expense, and executive performance reporting.
A successful candidate will combine deep financial expertise with strong business acumen, operational discipline, executive presence, and the ability to influence senior leaders across the company.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Work closely with the executive leadership team to develop short and long-term strategic business plans, annual operating budgets along with associated tracking and reporting. Proactively work with the executive leadership team in establishing appropriate spending levels and incentive programs to drive continued innovation while at the same time improving key operating metrics.
- Develop robust forecasting methodologies and processes to improve visibility into revenue, gross margin, operating expenses, free cash flow, and capital requirements.
- Provide rigorous financial analysis and decision support for major strategic initiatives, investments, acquisitions, capital allocation decisions, and other new ventures.
- Translate corporate strategy into actionable financial plans, performance targets, and resource allocation decisions (operating expense and capital expenditures).
- Providing insights and guidance into our various reporting processes, including executive level performance packages, management packages and Board of Directors material.
- Leading the development, monitoring and reporting of key operational metrics and driving processes to improve consistent productivity and efficiency improvements.
- Performing ad hoc financial analysis to support key business decisions.
- Working with internal teams to develop detailed peer reviews and competitive financial analysis.
- Support the quarterly earnings cycle in partnership with Investor Relations and Accounting, including guidance development, consensus and street-model reconciliation, and the financial narrative provided to external stakeholders.
- 15+ years relevant experience in Finance, Accounting or related fields in the technology industry.
- Strong analytical and business acumen, with a demonstrated ability to understand profitability drivers and to deliver financial results.
- A proven track record of process improvement including experience with financial systems and process change initiatives.
- Strong communication and relationship building skills at senior levels, with the ability to interpret and summarize data to aid management in achieving strategic and operational goals.
- Driven and ambitious attitude with a high energy level, growth mindset and passion for identifying and driving process improvements.
- Confidence and experience to take high level goals and develop and execute plans to achieve those goals.
- Excellent verbal and written communications skills.
- Confidence collaborating across all levels of the organization and with presenting to the executive leadership team.
- Ability to challenge the norms and existing processes and relentlessly look for ways to add value and to position the organization for success
- Ability to effectively manage projects.
- Expert level user of Excel, PowerPoint and modeling skills.

jobs.title: Global Trade Program Manager - C-TPAT
jobs.description:
The Global Customs Trade Programs & Supply Chain Programs Expert is a strategic program management role responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving a portfolio of global trade programs. The core focus spans Supply Chain Security (CTPAT/AEO), Environmental Sustainability, Record Retention and AI Enabled Compliance assurance program — with an open mandate to expand into additional customs trade program domains as the business evolves.
The ideal candidate brings a blend of strong program management expertise and deep subject matter knowledge in customs and trade programs expertise. They are a thought leader who can strategize, build governance frameworks, drive programs to completion, and adapt to an ever-changing regulatory landscape — leveraging AI tools and automation to work smarter, all while championing a culture of trade program awareness across the organization.
1.  Program Management & Execution
- Design and lead end-to-end program management for customs trade program initiatives including Supply Chain Security, Sustainability, Record retention and Compliance assurance programs — with the agility to onboard additional customs programs.
- Drive Western Digital to secure and maintain CTPAT Trade Compliance certification; support global sites in securing and/or retaining AEO certifications.
- Serve as liaison with internal team members and legal when faced with audits from CBP and other regulatory bodies;
- Evaluate and deploy AI-powered tools to streamline trade program workflows — including Supply Chain Security risk assessment, Compliance assurance program and across all managed programs.
- Integrate sustainability requirements into supply chain operations, ensuring alignment with internal ESG goals and external regulatory obligations.
- Institute robust governance models for all managed programs; participate actively in industry associations to benchmark and enhance program value.

2.  Compliance & Risk Management
- Conduct regular risk assessments and audits to identify and remediate vulnerabilities across the supply chain trade programs portfolio.
- Leverage AI-assisted monitoring tools to continuously scan for regulatory changes, supply chain anomalies, and emerging trade program risks in real time.
- Develop and maintain an Internal Control Program to ensure systemic trade program adherence across all program areas.
- Maintain readiness for regulatory inquiries, third-party audits, and certification renewals.

3.  Strategy & Continuous Improvement
- Act as a thought leader — define the strategic roadmap for each trade program, balancing near-term deliverables with long-term scalability.
- Identify and implement technology solutions to automate manual processes, reduce cost, and improve program effectiveness.
- Champion responsible AI adoption within trade program operations — define guardrails, evaluate vendor AI tools, and ensure AI use aligns with regulatory expectations and internal governance standards.
- Partner with IT and data teams to build AI/ML-powered dashboards and analytics that surface trade program trends, predict risk, and support executive decision-making.
- Analyze program performance data to surface improvement opportunities; drive structured continuous improvement cycles.
- Proactively identify adjacent customs trade program domains (e.g., trade programs, duty management, origin programs) and develop business cases to expand the program portfolio.

4.  Training, Awareness & Culture
- Design and deliver role-specific training programs for employees, suppliers, and stakeholders across all trade program domains.
- Champion a culture of trade program awareness and security awareness throughout the organization.
- Develop accessible playbooks, reference materials, and e-learning content to scale trade program knowledge.

5.  Cross-Functional & External Collaboration
- Partner closely with Logistics, Legal, IT, Finance, and Business Unit teams to embed trade program requirements into business operations seamlessly.
- Coordinate with suppliers, freight forwarders, customs brokers, and other external partners to ensure supply chain-wide adherence.
- Represent the organization in industry forums, regulatory working groups, and with government agencies.

6.  Documentation & Reporting
- Maintain comprehensive records of program activities: audits, risk assessments, certifications, and training.
- Prepare and submit required regulatory filings and reports to CBP and other relevant authorities.
- Provide executive-level reporting on program status, risks, and KPIs.
Education
- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, International Business, Business Administration, or a related field. Master's degree preferred.
- Certified Licensed Customs Broker (preferred).
- Certified Dangerous Goods Professional (DGR).
- Additional certifications in trade programs, sustainability, or program management (e.g., PMP) are a plus.

Experience
- 10+ years of experience managing global supply chain trade programs, including hands-on responsibility for at least two of: Supply Chain Security (CTPAT/AEO), Dangerous Goods (IATA/Hazmat), Supply Chain Sustainability, or customs trade programs.
- Demonstrated track record of building programs from the ground up — obtaining certifications, designing governance frameworks, and scaling operations.
- Experience working directly with customs authorities (e.g., CBP) and international regulatory bodies.
- Experience in technology-intensive supply chains, preferably in the semiconductor, electronics, or manufacturing sector.

Core Program Management Skills
- Ability to manage a portfolio of concurrent trade programs with competing priorities and stakeholders.
- Strong project planning, milestone tracking, risk management, and executive communication skills.
- Comfort operating in ambiguous environments — able to define scope, build structure, and execute with limited guidance.
- Change management and organizational influence skills; ability to drive adoption without direct authority.

Domain Expertise
- Deep knowledge of CTPAT requirements, AEO frameworks, and international trade security regulations.
- Expertise with supply chain sustainability standards (e.g., GHG Protocol, CDP, EU CSRD) and ESG reporting requirements.
- Broad understanding of global customs regulations, trade programs, classification, and valuation principles.

Technical & Interpersonal Skills
- Excellent executive communication and presentation skills — ability to distill complex regulatory topics for senior leadership.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities; data-driven approach to risk and performance management.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; familiarity with trade management systems (TMS), trade program platforms, or ERP systems is a plus.
- Hands-on experience with AI tools for trade program tasks — such as document review, risk scoring, regulatory change tracking, or automated reporting — strongly preferred.
- High learning agility and growth mindset — eager to take on new programs and expand expertise into emerging trade program domains.
Open Program Mandate
This role is designed to grow. While the initial focus areas are Supply Chain Security, Sustainability, and Compliance assurance, the incumbent is expected and encouraged  to proactively identify and take ownership of additional customs trade programs. As AI reshapes the trade programs landscape, this role is also at the forefront of deploying intelligent tools and defining responsible AI use in regulated supply chain operations. jobs.description:
The Senior Director, Finance - Data Center Segment serves as the principal finance executive for Western Digital's largest and most strategically critical business unit. This role drives the financial strategy, planning, forecasting, and performance management for a multi-billion-dollar Data Center product portfolio spanning enterprise HDD, nearline storage, and next-generation capacity storage solutions serving the world's leading hyperscale cloud providers, enterprise OEMs, and channel partners.
This leader operates at the intersection of finance, strategy, and commercial execution -translating complex market dynamics, customer demand signals, and product transitions into actionable financial insights that support executive decision-making at the highest levels of the organization. The Senior Director serves as a trusted advisor to Business Unit leadership and a critical partner to Corporate Finance, ensuring that segment performance is aligned with company-wide profitability objectives and long-range strategic goals.
Beyond financial stewardship, this role carries a significant leadership mandate - building, developing, and supporting a finance organization while establishing clear expectations, accountability, analytical rigor, and continuous improvement across all finance functions supporting the Data Center business.
Key Responsibilities
Financial Planning & Forecasting
- Own the end-to-end planning process - AOP, quarterly forecasts, monthly outlooks, and long-range plans
- Drive revenue and gross margin forecasting across all DC customer segments with a strong emphasis on accuracy and process discipline
- Partner with Sales, Business Planning, and Pricing to align forecasts with customer commitments, market share targets, and pricing strategy
- Translate macro trends - cloud CapEx cycles, AI infrastructure buildout, hyperscale demand - into quantified financial impact for executive planning

- Lead monthly business reviews with senior and C-suite leadership, delivering concise, insight-driven financial presentations
- Develop and maintain KPIs and dashboards covering revenue, gross margin, ASP trends, volume mix, and product profitability
- Identify performance gaps early and drive corrective action recommendations with cross-functional partners
- Build risk and opportunity frameworks that provide leadership with balanced, scenario-based financial outlooks

Strategic Finance & Business Partnership
- Serve as a strategic thought partner to the DC General Manager on all major business decisions
- Support product roadmap investments, customer deal economics, and market expansion opportunities with rigorous financial analysis and business case development
- Evaluate large customer agreements, pricing concessions, and supply commitments against margin thresholds and company objectives
- Provide financial framing for executive reviews, board presentations, and long-range planning sessions

- Experience leading finance for a business segment with direct accountability for P&L outcomes
- Demonstrated success building and leading effective finance teams
- Experience partnering with hyperscale, cloud, or enterprise technology customers on complex commercial engagements preferred

- Strong data analytics skills with proficiency in Excel, Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent analytical tools

- Working knowledge of AI-driven forecasting tools and modern FP&A technologies preferred
- Solid understanding of cost accounting, standard costing, and manufacturing economics

jobs.description:
Summary of the Role:
As a Lead Specialist IV, Process Excellence & Program Management (Lean Six Sigma Black Belt Certified), you will be responsible for leading the design, deployment and sustainment of continuous improvement and innovation programs across the Philippine Head Operations organization. The role serves as a key enabler of operational excellence by strengthening continuous improvement capabilities at the Professional and Manager levels and driving measurable business impact through structured methodologies, AI-augmented problem-solving, coaching, and a strong culture of innovation. The potential candidate is expected to be a forward-looking continuous improvement practitioner, combining proven CI frameworks with emerging AI-enabled tools and technologies to accelerate problem-solving, unlock breakthrough opportunities, and deliver sustainable performance improvements across the organization.
Key Responsibilities and Role Accountabilities:
I. Continuous Improvement Program Leadership
- Architect and own the end-to-end Process Excellence roadmap aligned to Head Backend Operations strategic priorities.
- Lead and facilitate improvement initiatives using structured methodologies like AI enabled Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and DMAIC frameworks across cross-functional teams.
- Define, track, and report program KPIs including cost savings, cycle time reduction, yield improvement, and defect elimination.
- Partner with Engineering, Quality, and Manufacturing teams to identify and prioritize high-impact improvement opportunities.

II. AI-Augmented Problem Solving
- Champion the integration of AI tools (generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics) into the standard problem-solving toolkit for Professionals and Managers.
- Apply AI-assisted root cause analysis using pattern recognition and anomaly detection models to accelerate diagnosis of complex, multi-variable manufacturing problems.
- Leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) and prompt engineering techniques to support structured ideation, failure mode analysis, and process documentation generation.

III. Innovation Enablement
- Champion structured innovation methodologies augmented by AI-powered ideation tools to generate and prioritize breakthrough ideas.
- Use AI-assisted brainstorming platforms and prompt frameworks to systematically unlock unconventional solutions from Professionals and Managers.
- Develop and manage innovation pipelines in collaboration with program owners; Manage ideation workflows.
- Integrate innovation platforms and tools with AI-generated prompt libraries to enhance idea quality and volume.
- Create safe-to-fail environments that encourage experimentation, AI-assisted prototyping, and rapid iteration.

IV. Mentoring & Capability Development
- Serve as a primary mentor and coach for Professionals and Managers in applying process improvement, problem-solving, and AI tools.
- Design and deliver structured mentoring programs including one-on-one coaching, group workshops, and on-the-job application support.
- Guide mentees through real-world improvement projects from problem definition to solution implementation and control — incorporating AI at appropriate stages of the DMAIC cycle.
- Assess individual capability gaps and create personalized development plans tied to CI and AI skill progression
- Build and sustain a certified practitioner pipeline across the organization

V. Training & Knowledge Management
- Develop and maintain a Process Excellence curriculum that integrates traditional CI tools with AI applications covering foundational to advanced topics for varying experience levels
- Facilitate workshops, simulations, and learning sessions on Lean tools, root cause analysis, statistical methods, AI-assisted analytics , and change management
- Curate and manage a centralized knowledge repository of best practices, project templates, AI prompt libraries, and lessons learned
- Drive cross-site knowledge sharing and benchmarking within the broader Western Digital Global Operations network

VI. Stakeholder Engagement & Culture Change
- Build influential relationships with senior leaders, functional managers, and front-line professionals to embed CI and AI-augmented thinking as standard practice
- Champion a continuous improvement and AI-enabled innovation mindset as a visible culture ambassador within the organization
- Communicate program progress and impact to Director and VP-level stakeholders through structured business reviews
- Recognize and celebrate improvement achievements to reinforce positive behaviors and sustain engagement
Education and Work Experience:
- Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Management, Organizational Development, Statistics or a related field of study.
- Academic or professional exposure to Lean Management, Six Sigma, Process Excellence, Data Analytics, Artificial Intelligence, or Innovation Management is highly desirable.
- Atleast 7 years of professional experience in a relevant field.
- Industry exposure in the Electronics or Semiconductor Manufacturing setup is highly preferred.
- Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification is required. Candidates with demonstrated Master Black Belt-level project experience are highly preferred.

jobs.title: サプライチェーンプログラムマネージャー (Supply Chain Program Manager-Strategic Sourcing & Procurement)
jobs.description:
＜採用ポジション＞
サプライチェーンプログラムマネージャー (Supply Chain Program Manager-Strategic Sourcing & Procurement)
＜職務内容＞
サプライチェーンプログラムマネージャーは、新規および既存製品のソーシング・調達、プロセス改善、サプライチェーン変革プログラムをリードします。関係部門間の連携を推進し、リスクを早期に特定・対処しながら、各プログラムを定められたスケジュール・スコープ内で完遂させ、ビジネスへの具体的な成果をもたらすことを責務とします。
この役割は、クロスファンクショナルな組織に対して幅広い視点でリーダーシップを発揮し、新製品がコスト、品質、機能性、スケジュール、生産目標を達成できるようリードします。ステークホルダーと緊密に連携し、製品調達計画、安定供給の維持、コスト目標について合意形成を図ります。また、各コモディティマネージャーと協力して、供給リスクを最小限に抑え、安定供給を実現する調達戦略を立案・実行を担います。
The Supply Chain Program Manager leads critical initiatives such as new product launches, capacity expansions, and transformation programs. This role drives alignment, mitigates risks, and ensures programs are delivered on time, within scope, and with measurable business impact.
This role provides expansive thought leadership across cross-functional teams to ensure new products meet cost, quality, functionality, schedule, and production objectives. The Supply Chain Program Manager works closely with senior stakeholders to align on product sourcing plans, supply continuity, and cost targets. Program manager partners with Global Commodity Managers to develop and implement sourcing strategies that minimize risk and ensure continuity of supply.
具体的な業務は以下の通り。
プログラムのリーダーシップと実行
- クロスファンクショナルなチームを率い、新製品立ち上げ（NPI）および量産継続プログラムにおける部材・コンポーネントの供給準備の推進
- 調達・購買領域におけるスコープ・スケジュール・リソース・予算のエンドツーエンドのプログラム管理のオーナーシップ
- 社内ガバナンスフレームワークおよびマイルストーンレビュープロセスの徹底

戦略的調達と計画立案
- 技術・供給・コスト・品質・供給体制の強靭性のギャップを解消するための調達戦略の策定・実行
- 新製品立ち上げ（NPI）プログラムにおける部材の段階的調達計画の策定、及び、円滑な量産移行
- 需要予測とサプライヤーのリードタイム分析を活用した在庫の最適配置
- コモディティマネージャーおよび戦略的コスト管理チームと連携し、製品コスト管理施策を主導

サプライヤー・パートナー管理
- コスト・品質・供給安定性・イノベーション・サステナビリティの観点からサプライヤーのパフォーマンスを管理
- 事業継続性確保のため、新規および代替サプライヤーの認定・承認
- 主要サプライヤーとともにVA/VEおよび継続的改善活動を推進
- 長期的な調達戦略を支える強固なサプライヤーとの信頼関係構築

プロセス改善とレポーティング
- リーンおよびシックスシグマの手法を活用した継続的な業務改善の推進
- プログラムの成果指標・KPIを策定し、ステークホルダーへの定期的報告
- アフターアクションレビューを実施し、知見を集約してプロセス改善に反映

ステークホルダーエンゲージメント
- エンジニアリング・品質・製造・生産計画・購買・NPI／量産継続プログラム管理の各チームとの連携
- サプライチェーン戦略、プログラムの進捗状況を、各ビジネスファンクション・経営陣に発信・共有
- ステアリングコミッティおよび経営陣向けレビューフォーラムの運営サポート

Key Responsibilities

Program Leadership & Execution
- Lead cross-functional teams to ensure material and component readiness for NPI and sustaining programs
- Own end-to-end program management of scope, schedule, resources, and budget across sourcing and procurement workstreams
- Ensure compliance with internal governance frameworks and milestone review processes

Strategic Sourcing & Planning
- Define and execute sourcing strategies to close gaps in technology, supply, cost, quality, and resiliency
- Develop material ramp plans for NPI programs and manage transitions to mass production
- Optimize inventory positioning using demand forecasts and supplier lead-time analysis
- Lead product cost management initiatives in partnership with Global Commodity Managers and Strategic Cost Management teams

Supplier & Partner Management
- Drive supplier performance across cost, quality, resiliency, innovation, and sustainability objectives
- Facilitate qualification of new and alternate suppliers to support business continuity
- Lead VA/VE and continuous improvement initiatives with key supply partners
- Build and maintain strong supplier relationships to support long-term sourcing strategies

Process Improvement & Reporting
- Drive continuous improvement using Lean and Six Sigma methodologies
- Develop, track, and communicate program metrics and KPIs to senior stakeholders
- Conduct after-action reviews to capture learnings and implement process improvements

Stakeholder Engagement
- Collaborate with Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Planning, Procurement, and NPI/Sustaining Program Management teams
- Communicate supply chain strategies and program status to business units and leadership
- Support steering committees and executive review forums

Skills & Competencies
Technical
Strategic sourcing & supplier management

NPI/program management

Risk management & supply continuity

Data analysis & forecasting

ERP systems & digital tools
Leadership & Workplace
Problem-solving & decision-making

Cross-functional collaboration

Conflict resolution

Planning & organizing
Personal Effectiveness
Clear communication & executive presence

Integrity & accountability

Continuous learning & adaptability

- ベストプラクティスに基づく調達手法を活用した、部材・資材プログラムマネジメントの経験

Western Digital's presence across APAC spans a diverse set of markets, cultures, and business contexts — and this role sits at the center of it all. As the Director of Talent Development and Inclusion for APAC, you will serve as the regional leader for our global Talent, Development and Inclusion function, translating enterprise strategy into locally relevant programs and that build stronger leaders, more effective managers, and more engaged drivers who can deliver for our business.
You will lead a small team embedded across key APAC locations, partnering closely with HR and business leaders to deliver development experiences that reflect both global standards and regional nuance. We are looking for a strategic and hands on Director, People Technology to lead a team of Business Systems Analysts responsible for delivering scalable, business focused technology solutions across People functions. This leader will mentor and grow a high performing business analysis team. This team is responsible for translating business needs into effective process and technology solutions across HR domains.
The ideal candidate combines strong people leadership, deep business analysis expertise, systems thinking, and a passion for developing talent. This role sits at the forefront of delivering high-quality outcomes across the People Technology portfolio.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITES
Team Leadership
This role leads, mentors, and develops a team of Business Systems Analysts by fostering accountability, continuous improvement, collaboration, and user centric problem solving. The Director establishes clear expectations, creates meaningful development plans, and opens career growth opportunities for team members while defining the capabilities and skills required for a strong business systems analysis function. Just as importantly, this leader builds a culture of knowledge sharing, constructive challenge, innovation, and impact.
Technology Leadership
The Director is responsible for driving our HR technology vision, roadmap, and execution. They provide direction and oversight across the full tech lifecycle, including requirements discovery, process analysis, functional design, testing, implementation, and post-launch optimization. This leader ensures consistent standards for documentation, quality controls, and delivery methods across the team, while coaching analysts to translate complex business challenges into clear, scalable, and sustainable process and technology solutions. The role also requires functional and technical depth to evaluate tradeoffs, challenge solution approaches, and engage credibly with business and technology partners.
Stakeholder Partnership
This leader serves as a trusted advisor to the People team, our IT technology partners, and company cross-functional stakeholders. The Director owns strong relationships across the organization to understand strategy, clarify priorities, and identify opportunities for transformation and optimization. They facilitate complex discussions, resolve ambiguity, align stakeholders, and drive decisions on requirements and solution direction, while creating transparency around priorities, dependencies, risks, tradeoffs, and expected business outcomes.
Improvement & Innovation
This leader drives continuous improvement through process simplification, standardization, automation, and thoughtful technology enablement. They encourage the team to identify root causes, question legacy practices, and recommend solutions that improve employee experiences. They also champion responsible adoption of emerging capabilities and new ways of working to create measurable business value.
Required:

•  Strong understanding of enterprise HR technology, the HR domain, and its processes. The ability to connect company business priorities to HR programs and deliver meaningful, impactful outcomes.

•   Expertise in modern SaaS HR systems architecture, integration principles, data quality practices, and emerging technologies such as AI.
•   Significant experience and ability in designing and then delivering multi-year roadmaps, balancing quick wins with longer term transformative work.
•  Exceptional communication, facilitation, influencing, stakeholder management, and problem solving skills.
About you:
•  The People Gardener. You elevate capability through clear expectations, candid coaching, meaningful opportunities, and active investment in team growth. You’re known for growing future leaders.
•  The Cartographer. You are comfortable operating in ambiguity and building as you go. If the map doesn’t exist you make it.
• The Dot Connector. You analyze processes, data, user experience, technology, and operating realities before recommending a path forward. You understand both technology and HR deeply enough to keep the focus on business outcomes and employee experience. You deliver user-centric holistic outcomes, not fragmented bodies of work.
•  The Smooth Operator. You know when to create repeatable structure and when to remain agile. You know when to slow down and when to speed up. You deliver amazing outcomes and build durable scale with just the right depth of structure and controls.
•  The Bridge Builder. You build credibility across functions, communicate clearly, and create alignment even when priorities or perspectives differ. You are viewed as a respected and trusted partner no matter the situation. You help stakeholders first envision and then move from current to future state.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Marketing Operations
jobs.description:
About the Role
We're looking for a Senior Manager of Marketing Operations to be the operational backbone of our Corporate Marketing organization — and a close operating partner to the VP of Corporate Marketing. This person will own our budget, drive our semi-annual planning process, bring rigor to how we use data and analytics, and act as a chief of staff across the org: helping prioritize, coordinate, and keep cross-functional work moving.
This is a high-visibility, high-trust role designed for someone with the capability and ambition to grow in the role over time. We're looking for someone who already operates with Executive-level judgment -  who can walk into ambiguity, build the system that's missing, and represent the marketing organization credibly with Finance, cross-functional partners and senior leadership.
What You'll Do
1. Own Budget & Financial Stewardship
- Own the Corporate Marketing budget end-to-end: tracking, forecasting, variance analysis, and reconciliation across the fiscal year.
- Partner directly with Finance on budget planning, quarterly reviews, and reforecasts -  translating marketing priorities into financial terms Finance trusts.
- Build visibility into spend by function and campaign so leadership always has an accurate, current view of where investment is going and what it's returning.
- Flag risk early: over/under-spend trends, vendor commitments, and budget reallocation needs, before they become a surprise.
- Establish disciplined spend governance across vendors, agencies, POs and commitments, ensuring forecast reflects both actual and committed spend.

2. Drive Semi-Annual Planning
- Own and run the semi-annual planning process for the Corporate Marketing organization end-to-end: timeline, templates, cross-functional input, and synthesis into a single, coherent plan.
- Partner with each function lead (Brand, Integrated Campaigns & Content, PR/AR, Product & Technical Marketing) to translate goals into resourced, sequenced plans.
- Build the planning cadence into a repeatable system not a one-off scramble each cycle, with clear inputs, owners, and deadlines.

3. Bring Rigor to Analytics & Insight
- Own the Corporate Marketing Monthly Report end-to-end gathering inputs across the organization, validating the underlying data, identifying the insights and implications that matter, and translating performance into a concise executive narrative.
- Own the operating cadence for marketing scorecards and KPI reporting, including ELT-level reporting cycles, ensuring metrics are consistent, accurate and decision-useful.
- Interpret and stress-test the data our analytics team provides. You won't be pulling the reports yourself, but you need to understand them well enough to catch what's wrong, ask the hard questions, and push back when something doesn't add up.
- Translate data into recommendations, not just dashboards connecting marketing performance metrics to business outcomes leadership actually cares about.
- Partner with the analytics team as a rigorous internal customer: defining what should be measured, sanity-checking methodology, and ensuring KPIs reported upward are accurate and defensible.

4. Build Marketing Operations Infrastructure & Systems Readiness
- Establish and govern campaign measurement standards including UTM taxonomy, naming conventions, campaign tracking and data hygiene so performance can be measured consistently across channels and over time.
- Partner with Integrated Campaigns & Content and Analytics to ensure campaigns are instrumented correctly and measurement is designed upfront, not retrofitted after launch.
- Bring hands-on Salesforce and Marketo experience and a strong point of view on marketing systems, lead lifecycle, and campaign infrastructure.
- Serve as the person who could stand up or evolve these systems if/when WD adopts them more broadly. This isn't a day-one need, but we want that capability on the team so we're not starting from zero when the moment comes.
- In the meantime, apply that systems-thinking background to how we operate today: process design, tooling evaluation, and marketing operations best practices generally.

5. Act as Chief of Staff to the Function Leader
- Establish and manage the operating cadence for Corporate Marketing connecting annual and semi-annual planning, monthly performance reviews, budget reviews, leadership meetings, scorecards and follow-through into a coherent management rhythm.
- Help prioritize and sequence what gets attention across a broad, fast-moving organization, spanning Press & Analyst Relations, Product & Technical Marketing, Integrated Campaigns & Content, Brand Strategy & Experiences, International Marketing, and Marketing Operations.
- Prepare materials and talking points for executive and board-level conversations, and help synthesize input from across the function into clear, decision-ready recommendations.
- Represent the leader's priorities in cross-functional forums and follow through on action items and commitments across teams.
- Take on special projects that don't have a natural home elsewhere - org design questions, process gaps, ad hoc executive requests - and see them through.

What Success Looks Like
- Budget is accurate, current, and defensible, no surprises at quarter-end.
- The semi-annual planning process runs on a system, not heroics, and produces a plan leadership trusts.
- Data reported upward is accurate, and leadership trusts this person's read on what the numbers actually mean.
- The marketing organization operates with more discipline and less ad hoc scrambling than it did a year prior.
- This person is trusted with ambiguity, handed a loosely defined problem and expected to structure it, not asked to wait for instructions.
What We're Looking For
Must-Have Experience
- 7–10+ years in marketing operations, revenue operations, or a related operational/analytical role, ideally within a complex or matrixed B2B organization.
- Strong analytical fluency: able to understand data sources, methodologies, attribution approaches and KPI definitions well enough to challenge assumptions, identify inconsistencies and distinguish signal from noise.
- Hands-on experience with Salesforce and Marketo (or comparable marketing automation/CRM platforms) even if not immediately applied here, this experience needs to be real and current enough to be credible.
- Strong track record owning a budget of meaningful size, including forecasting and variance management, and partnering directly with Finance.
- Demonstrated ability to design and run a planning process for a function or organization, not just participate in one.

Core Capabilities
Operational Rigor
- Builds systems and processes that scale, rather than relying on one-off effort each cycle.
- Comfortable being the person who brings structure to ambiguity.

Analytical Judgment
- Can interpret data critically, spot inconsistencies, and ask the hard question rather than taking a number at face value.
- Translates data into a recommendation, not just a report.

Executive Judgment & Trust
- Exercises discretion and sound judgment operating close to senior leadership.
- Communicates clearly and concisely, in a way that's ready for executive consumption.

Business & Financial Acumen
- Understands how marketing investment connects to business priorities and can make thoughtful tradeoffs across competing needs.
- Comfortable moving between marketing language, financial language and executive-level business discussions.

Cross-Functional Influence
- Earns credibility and cooperation from function leads without formal authority over them.
- Comfortable pushing back constructively when priorities conflict.

What Sets You Apart
- You've run a budget and a planning process before, and you have opinions about what worked and what didn't.
- You ask “where did this number come from” as a reflex, not an afterthought.
- You've supported a senior leader in a chief-of-staff-like capacity and understand the difference between administrative support and operating partnership.

jobs.title: Deputy Chief Compliance Officer
jobs.description:
The Deputy Chief Compliance Officer serves as the Chief Compliance Officer’s principal deputy and is responsible for overseeing the operational execution of the company’s global Ethics & Compliance program. This executive oversees the day-to-day management of core compliance functions, ensuring that programs operate effectively, consistently, and in alignment with legal requirements, regulatory expectations, and the company’s values.
The Deputy Chief Compliance Officer provides strategic and operational oversight of compliance operations, investigations, anti-corruption compliance, ethics reporting, employee training, and compliance communications while helping build and sustain a culture of integrity across the organization. The role serves as the Chief Compliance Officer’s delegate on key initiatives and governance activities and oversees a high-performing compliance team.
Experience in international trade compliance, privacy, data protection, and artificial intelligence governance is highly desirable.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Compliance Operations and Program Management
- Oversee the day-to-day operation of the global Ethics & Compliance program.
- Translate compliance strategy into operational plans, measurable objectives, and effective execution.
- Develop and manage annual compliance work plans, budgets, metrics, and performance dashboards.
- Establish clear roles, processes, service expectations, and accountability across the compliance team.
- Drive continuous improvement across compliance processes, technology, reporting, and governance.
- Establish scalable processes that support business growth and evolving regulatory expectations.
- Coordinate compliance risk assessments, program reviews, monitoring, testing, and remediation activities.
- Prepare executive and Board-level compliance reports and presentations.
- Serve as the Chief Compliance Officer’s delegate on designated committees, initiatives, and leadership matters.

Ethics Reporting and Whistleblower Program
Oversee the company’s global ethics reporting and whistleblower program, including:
- Ethics hotline, web-based reporting, and other speak-up channels.
- Case intake, assessment, triage, assignment, escalation, and closure.
- Case-management systems, processes, documentation, and quality standards.
- Oversight of hotline and case-management vendors.
- Reporting analytics, trend identification, and root-cause analysis.
- Speak-up culture initiatives and employee awareness.
- Retaliation prevention, monitoring, and response.
- Confidentiality, data privacy, and regulatory reporting requirements.
- Reporting of significant matters to senior leadership and appropriate Board committees.
- Ensure that concerns are handled promptly, objectively, consistently, confidentially, and in accordance with company policy and applicable law.

Investigations
Oversee the global compliance investigations function, including investigations involving:
- Code of Conduct violations.
- Bribery and corruption.
- Fraud, theft, and financial misconduct.
- Conflicts of interest.
- Retaliation.
- Third-party misconduct.
- Books-and-records or internal-controls concerns.
- Misuse of company assets or information.
- Trade, privacy, data, or technology-related compliance concerns, as appropriate.
- Other significant legal, ethical, or reputational risks.

Additional responsibilities include:
- Establish investigation protocols, documentation requirements, and quality standards.
- Ensure appropriate independence, objectivity, confidentiality, and consistency.
- Oversee internal investigators, cross-functional investigation teams, and outside counsel.
- Ensure investigations are timely, thorough, well documented, and defensible.
- Coordinate with Human Resources, Legal, Internal Audit, Security, and other functions.
- Identify root causes, systemic issues, and appropriate corrective actions.
- Promote consistent disciplinary and remediation practices.
- Present significant matters to executive leadership and Board committees, as appropriate.
- Track investigation trends and use findings to improve policies, controls, training, and organizational culture.

Anti-Corruption Compliance
Oversee the company’s global anti-bribery and anti-corruption compliance program, including:
- Compliance with the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, UK Bribery Act, and other applicable anti-corruption laws.
- Gifts, meals, travel, entertainment, and hospitality controls.
- Interactions with government officials and state-owned enterprises.
- Charitable contributions, political contributions, sponsorships, and community investments.
- Third-party anti-corruption due diligence, contracting, monitoring, and remediation.
- Anti-corruption risk assessments.
- Books-and-records and internal-controls requirements.
- Mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, and other transaction-related anti-corruption diligence and integration.
- Risk-based monitoring and testing of anti-corruption controls.
- Investigation and remediation of potential anti-corruption concerns.

Partner with Legal, Finance, Internal Audit, Procurement, Sales, Human Resources, and business leaders to identify, assess, and mitigate corruption risks globally.
Compliance Training and Communications
Oversee the company’s ethics and compliance education and communications strategy, including:
- Annual Code of Conduct training.
- Risk-based compliance training.
- Anti-corruption training.
- Manager and leadership education.
- Investigator and case-management training.
- Speak-up and non-retaliation communications.
- New employee onboarding.
- Policy launches and targeted communications.
- Compliance awareness campaigns.
- Training for higher-risk functions, geographies, and employee populations.

Oversee the development of practical, engaging, accessible, and measurable learning experiences that strengthen ethical decision-making and help employees understand how compliance requirements apply to their work.
Establish metrics to evaluate training completion, employee understanding, behavioral impact, and opportunities for improvement.
Team Operations and Oversight
- Oversee the operations, performance, and development of the compliance team.
- Establish clear objectives, priorities, performance expectations, and accountability.
- Support team capability building, professional development, and succession planning.
- Promote collaboration across regional and functional teams.
- Allocate resources according to risk and business priorities.
- Foster a culture of integrity, inclusion, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
- Support the Chief Compliance Officer in organizational planning and talent development across the broader compliance function.

Cross-Functional Leadership
Partner closely with:
- Legal.
- International Trade Compliance.
- Privacy and Data Protection.
- Artificial Intelligence and Data Governance.
- Internal Audit.
- Human Resources.
- Finance.
- Information Security.
- Corporate Security.
- Enterprise Risk Management.
- Procurement.
- Internal Communications.
- Government Affairs.
- Business and regional leadership.

Serve as a trusted advisor on ethics and compliance matters and help promote coordinated governance across legal, regulatory, data, technology, and enterprise-risk functions.
Support for Adjacent Governance Areas
Although the role’s principal responsibilities are compliance operations, training, the whistleblower program, investigations, and anti-corruption, the Deputy Chief Compliance Officer may also support the Chief Compliance Officer in adjacent areas, including:
- International trade compliance, export controls, sanctions, customs, and antiboycott matters.
- Privacy and data-protection governance.
- Artificial intelligence and responsible AI governance.
- Data governance and emerging technology risk.
- Cross-functional regulatory risk assessments.
- Governance committees and enterprise-wide risk initiatives.
- Coordination among legal, compliance, privacy, security, data, and technology stakeholders.

The level of responsibility in these areas will depend on the successful candidate’s experience and the evolving needs of the organization.
Governance, Metrics, and Reporting
- Develop meaningful compliance key performance indicators and key risk indicators.
- Provide regular program updates to executive leadership.
- Support reporting to the Board of Directors and appropriate Board committees.
- Monitor regulatory developments, enforcement trends, and emerging compliance risks.
- Oversee compliance documentation, recordkeeping, and evidence of program effectiveness.
- Support periodic compliance program assessments and benchmarking.
- Use hotline, investigation, training, monitoring, and other data to identify trends and recommend improvements.
- Assist the Chief Compliance Officer in establishing an integrated view of compliance and regulatory risk
- Bachelor’s degree required; Juris Doctor or other relevant advanced degree preferred.
- At least 12 years of progressively responsible experience in ethics and compliance, legal, investigations, risk management, or a related field.
- Significant experience overseeing or managing a global or multinational compliance program.
- Demonstrated experience in:
- Compliance program operations.
- Corporate investigations.
- Ethics reporting and whistleblower systems.
- Anti-bribery and anti-corruption compliance.
- Compliance training and communications.
- Program metrics, governance, and executive reporting.
- Experience managing and developing compliance professionals.
- Strong executive presence, judgment, and communication skills.
- Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders and collaborate across functions and geographies.
- Ability to handle sensitive and confidential matters with discretion and objectivity.
- Experience managing complex projects and translating strategy into execution.
- Daily presence (Monday, Wednesday and Thursday) in office; periodically on Tuesday or Friday. This is not a remote role.

Preferred Qualifications
- Juris Doctor, master’s degree, or other relevant advanced degree.
- Certified Compliance & Ethics Professional, Certified Fraud Examiner, or comparable professional certification.
- Experience in a multinational technology, manufacturing, or other highly regulated company.
- Experience working with executive leadership, Boards of Directors, or Board committees.
- Familiarity with the U.S. Department of Justice’s guidance on the evaluation of corporate compliance programs, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines, and other recognized compliance frameworks.
- Experience with international trade compliance, including export controls, economic sanctions, customs, or antiboycott requirements.
- Experience with privacy, data protection, or data governance programs.
- Experience with artificial intelligence governance, responsible AI, algorithmic risk, or emerging technology compliance.
- Experience coordinating across compliance, legal, trade, privacy, information security, data, and technology functions.
- Familiarity with compliance technology, case-management systems, data analytics, automation, and technology-enabled monitoring.

As part of the dynamic, results-oriented Corporate Marketing organization, the Senior Manager, Brand Strategy plays a critical role within WD’s Brand Strategy & Experience team. This role is responsible for defining WD’s brand strategy and narrative, ensuring clarity, consistency, and scalability across enterprise and consumer portfolios.
The primary objective of this role is to develop and operationalize WD’s brand positioning, messaging architecture, and narrative frameworks , enabling consistent brand expression across a decentralized global organization. This individual serves as a strategic and hands-on leader who connects business priorities to compelling brand platforms and scalable execution systems.
WD is the storage foundation of the AI-driven data economy, powering innovation across enterprise infrastructure and consumer technology. jobs.description:
＜採用ポジション＞
人材開発マネージャー (Learning and Development Manager)
＜職務内容＞
ウエスタンデジタルの Talent, Development and Inclusion チームでは、組織としての競争力を維持するために必要な能力開発を担当します。今回募集する人材開発マネージャーは、日本における学習ニーズの把握から企画・実行までを一貫して担当し、グローバルの優先事項を日本のビジネス環境に適した形で落とし込み、全社員の能力向上を支援します。

また、本ポジションは APACの  Talent Development and Inclusion Director  にレポートし、グローバルチームと連携しながら、日本国内の全組織に対する学習・人材開発をリードする重要な役割です。

具体的な業務内容は以下の通り。

・ビジネスリーダーと連携し、日本における学習ニーズをグローバルの優先事項や組織変革の方向性との調整

・HRBPなどの日本のHRチームと協働し、日本特有の課題に対応したプログラムを企画

・シニアステークホルダーに対し、事業成果に直結する能力開発・研修の提案

・知識・スキル・行動面のギャップを分析し、短期・中長期の学習ロードマップの策定

・対面／オンライン研修やEラーニングなどの複合的学習ソリューションを設計・提供

・日本語／英語での研修を実施し、グローバル教材を日本の慣習に合わせてローカライズ

・研修効果を定量・定性指標で測定し、日本のHRチームと連携して改善を推進

・グローバル Talent Development and Inclusion チームと協働し、日本市場の知見を提供しつつ、グローバル基準に沿った学習フレームワークの展開

・外部ベンダーを選定・管理し、日本向けに提供されるコンテンツの品質と適合性の担保
Role Overview
The Talent, Development and Inclusion team at Western Digital is responsible for building the organizational capabilities that keep the company competitive — and right now, that means ensuring every employee has the skills needed to grow their career. The Learning and Development Manager – Japan will own the end-to-end learning assessment and delivery for WD's Japan workforce, translating global priorities into practical, locally resonant programs that build real capability at every level of the organization. This role works closely with Japan business leaders and the global Talent, Development and Inclusion team to identify where the gaps are, design solutions that close them, and measure whether the learning is effective in building and using both professional and technical skills.
This role will report to the Director, Talent Development and Inclusion, Asia-Pacific Region and is an incredible opportunity to be part of a global team and partnering on global programs while also having accountability for learning and development for all teams in Japan.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
- Partner with Japan business unit leaders to align the local learning needs with WD's global priorities and organizational transformation objectives
- Work closely with HR business partner, HR experience partner and Operation partner to address challenges in Japan, ensuring programs are relevant to the Japan business context.
- Advise senior Japan stakeholders on training needed for workforce readiness, translating capability into practical learning recommendations that connect directly to business performance and competitive positioning.
- Analyze Japan-specific capability gaps knowledge, skills and behaviors; develop a multi-year learning roadmap that supports both immediate needs and long-term business objectives.
- Design and deliver blended learning solutions — including in-person workshops, virtual instructor-led sessions, and self-directed digital content across Japan employee populations at all levels.
- Facilitate learning experiences in both Japanese and English, adapting global curriculum to reflect Japan workplace norms, communication styles, and learner expectations.
- Measure learning effectiveness through defined metrics — completion rates, behavioral indicators and manager-reported capability change — and monitor progress in partnership with Japan HR team.
- Coordinate with the global Talent Development and Inclusion team to localize enterprise learning frameworks, contributing Japan market insight to global program design while maintaining consistency with WD's global learning standards.
- Identify and manage external learning vendors or content partners where in-house capacity requires supplementation, owning the quality and relevance of any third-party learning content deployed in Japan.
＜必須となる経験、資格、スキル＞
・大卒相当以上

・教育、能力開発、人材開発、またはそれに関連するHR業域において5年以上の経験を有すること

・上記経験の内、教育プログラムの設計やビジネスリーダーへのアドバイザリー経験を3年以上有すること

・組織規模に応じた能力ギャップを解消する学習プログラムの設計・提供経験

・日本語：ネイティブレベル

・英語：ビジネスレベル（グローバルチームとの協働に必要）

・シニアビジネスリーダーとの信頼関係構築能力、および、事業課題を学習施策に落とし込むスキル
＜あれば望ましいスキル＞
・テクノロジー導入やDXに関連する学習プログラムの設計経験

・ADDIE、デザイン思考などといった研修設計手法の理解

・グローバルマトリクス組織での勤務経験

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Education, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience
- 5–10 years of experience in Learning and Development, Talent Development, or a closely related HR function, with at least 3 years focused on program design and stakeholder advisory work
- Demonstrated experience designing and delivering learning programs that address capability gaps at scale
- Native or near-native Japanese language proficiency; business-level English proficiency sufficient for global collaboration and cross-functional communication with WD's global teams
- Proven ability to build trusted working relationships with senior business leaders and translate business priorities into learning solutions

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience designing learning programs for technology adoption or digital transformation initiatives
- Exposure to instructional design methodologies (e.g., ADDIE, design thinking for learning) and adult learning principles applied to technical subject matter
- Experience working in a global matrixed organization and coordinating with geographically distributed HR or L&D teams
- Coaching or facilitation certification relevant to adult learning
- Experience in a mid-to-large multinational technology or manufacturing company

- Ability to assess organizational capability gaps and translate findings into structured, prioritized learning roadmaps — not generic training calendars
- Skill in adapting global learning content to Japan cultural and workplace norms without losing the intent or quality of the original design
- Ability to communicate learning to technical and non-technical learners across seniority levels, in both Japanese and English
- Comfort operating with ambiguity in an evolving program space — learning and development in Japan is a new role and this will require building infrastructure, not inheriting it

jobs.title: Senior Financial Analyst
jobs.description:
The Financial Analyst will partner with Business Unit teams and Finance leadership to provide financial analysis and insights that support informed business decisions. The role will analyze and interpret financial and operating results, identify key business drivers, and communicate findings to stakeholders.
Key responsibilities include PVMC analysis, forecasting and variance analysis, revenue and margin forecasting, ROI analysis for new product initiatives, and ad hoc financial analysis supporting Business Unit operations.
The Financial Analyst will also evaluate existing financial processes and systems, identify opportunities for improvement, document requirements, and help develop scalable analytical tools and processes that improve efficiency and support business growth.
Essential Functions
- Support monthly financial forecasting and planning activities.
- Support consolidation of weekly risks and opportunities (R&O).
- Prepare quarter-end financial reporting and analysis.
- Support management reporting and business reviews.
- Perform PVMC, revenue, margin, and profitability analysis.
- Develop variance and bridge analyses comparing actual results with forecasts and plans.
- Prepare ad hoc financial analyses and consolidated reporting for management review.
- Translate complex financial and operational data into clear, actionable insights for business partners and Finance leadership.
- Present analysis and recommendations to stakeholders in a clear, concise, and collaborative manner.
- Partner cross-functionally to identify business drivers, risks, opportunities, and potential financial impacts.
- Document existing methodologies and work with team members to identify opportunities for process improvement and automation.
- Perform gap analyses of financial systems, reporting tools, and processes, and document requirements for improvement.
- Apply financial insights to support business decisions related to profitability, efficiency, investment, and anticipated returns.
- Manage assigned deliverables and communicate progress, risks, and results to appropriate stakeholders.
Required
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience .
- Relevant experience in financial planning and analysis, forecasting, financial reporting, or a related finance function.
- Strong understanding of financial concepts, including revenue, gross margin, profitability, and P&L.
- Experience with forecasting, variance analysis, and financial modeling.
- Working knowledge of GAAP principles and financial reporting concepts.
- Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and experience working with large or complex datasets.
- Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify business drivers and translate analysis into actionable insights.

jobs.title: Operations Supervisor, Production
jobs.description:
The FQAP Supervisor oversees the Final Quality Assurance & Pending (FQAP) operations within WD Penang's HDD media component manufacturing environment. This role is responsible for leading a mixed team comprising Senior Leaders, Leaders, Technicians, Coordinators, and Operators to ensure all products meet WD quality and production standards. The Supervisor drives day-to-day floor operations, enforces process discipline, and collaborates with Engineering to resolve quality issues.
Key Responsibilities
- Supervise and coordinate daily FQAP operations across shifts, managing a team of Leaders, Technicians, Coordinators, and Operators.
- Meet daily shipment as per Dept objective
- Monitor production and quality output; track key metrics (parts transaction targets, throughput) and escalate issues promptly.
- Lead PI Count
- Lead root cause analysis (RCA) and corrective/preventive actions (CAPA) for quality non-conformances and escapes.
- Ensure adherence to SOPs, Work Instructions, and process control plans on the production floor.
- Conduct shift handovers, team briefings, and coordinate manpower planning and scheduling.
- Coach, develop, and assess team members including Technicians, Coordinators, Leaders, and Operators.
- Liaise with Manufacturing Engineering and Process teams to implement process improvements and resolve technical issues.
- Maintain audit readiness; ensure ESD, safety, and cleanroom compliance at all times.
- Prepare and present shift/daily performance reports to the Manager.
Education: Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or related technical field
Experience: Minimum 2–3 years of experience in manufacturing operations, production, technical training, or learning and development within a manufacturing environment.
Supervisory: Min. 2 years leading a production or quality team (Technicians, Operators, Leaders)
Technical Skills: Familiar with SPC, FMEA, RCA/CAPA, and production floor control systems
Systems: Working knowledge of MES/ERP systems; proficient in MS Office
